Frequently Asked Questions

Find answers to common questions about our firm and legal services. Don't see what you're looking for? Contact us directly.

We provide comprehensive legal services across multiple practice areas including Corporate Law, Commercial Litigation, Estate Planning, Real Estate, Employment Law, and Intellectual Property. Our attorneys serve businesses and individuals with sophisticated counsel tailored to their specific needs.
You can schedule a consultation by calling our office at (212) 555-0147, filling out the contact form on our website, or sending an email to contact@sterlingassociates.com. Initial consultations are typically scheduled within one week of your request.
Please bring any relevant documents related to your matter, such as contracts, correspondence, court papers, or financial records. Also bring a form of identification and a list of questions you'd like to discuss. The more information you provide, the better we can assess your situation.
Our fee structures vary depending on the type of matter. We offer hourly billing, flat fees for certain services, and alternative fee arrangements when appropriate. During your initial consultation, we will discuss the fee structure that best fits your needs and provide a clear understanding of expected costs.
Yes, while our primary office is in New York City, we represent clients across the United States and internationally. We are admitted to practice in multiple jurisdictions and work with a network of correspondent firms to serve clients wherever their legal needs arise.
The attorney-client privilege is a legal protection that keeps communications between you and your attorney confidential. This means we cannot disclose your information to third parties without your consent. The privilege encourages open communication so we can provide the most effective representation.
The timeline varies significantly depending on the complexity of your matter and the specific circumstances. Some transactions close within weeks, while litigation may take months or years. We will provide a realistic assessment of the expected timeline during your initial consultation and keep you informed of progress throughout.
Generally, we cannot represent both parties in the same transaction due to potential conflicts of interest. Our ethical obligations require us to avoid situations where our loyalty to one client could be compromised. If a conflict arises, we will discuss it with you and may need to decline representation.
